correctness.rationale: Exact two-point Rademacher Rayleigh distribution proves bias and variance for all 2x2 SPD orientations and every integer probe count. The sign of the continuous risk derivative is governed by the strictly increasing \(H(t)=U(t)/(rtB(t))\), which has limits \(2/B_0\) and infinity; thus only endpoint maxima and a unique possible interior minimum occur. This establishes both sharp critical sample thresholds with all equality and boundary cases. The 80,540 finite checks test, but do not replace, this analytic proof.

value.rationale: The exact two-dimensional benchmark exposes a practically meaningful bias floor that adding probes cannot defeat, despite vanishing stochastic variance, and sharply distinguishes the two sampling thresholds for best versus worst coordinate orientations. The motivated complete optimization addresses how one-step Krylov depth and probe budget interact; it is not a claimed high-dimensional algorithm or arbitrary isolated numerical sample. The precise limiting constants can guide sanity checks of general SLQ estimates.
